name: Ted Tosterud

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Tosterud lists his occupation as retired and past work at Quest Diagnostics and as owner of Northwest Medical Laboratories.
bio.excerpt: Direction of Operations; Quest Diagnostics, Inc. Owner Northwest Medical Laboratories Inc.;

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists a BS in chemistry from Portland State University.
bio.excerpt: Portland State University, BS in Chemistry

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists service as Fairview mayor and councilor and on Fairview and Multnomah County Sheriff budget committees.
bio.excerpt: Fairview Mayor; Fairview City Councilor; Fairview Budget Committee; Multnomah County Sheriff's Budget Committee

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Tosterud says he supports a moratorium on local fee and tax increases where feasible and transparent budgeting.
positions.excerpt: I support a moratorium on local fees and tax increases wherever feasible, and I will insist on transparent budgeting

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: His pamphlet statement says he will evaluate the Gresham Fire and Multnomah County Sheriff contract renewals.
positions.excerpt: I will carefully evaluate the Gresham Fire and Multnomah County Sheriff's contract renewals

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: His pamphlet statement says Fairview needs new retail businesses to grow its tax base without raising residents' taxes.
positions.excerpt: Fairview also needs new retail businesses to grow its tax base without raising taxes on residents.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: His pamphlet statement says that as mayor until 2019 he left the city financially stable and paid off water bond debt.
positions.excerpt: As Mayor until 2019, I left the city financially stable with adequate reserves: we paid off our water bond debt,

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: His pamphlet statement says he helped bring $33 million in development combining affordable housing with retail space.
